summary.text: Michael "Misha" Novakhov is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent in Assembly District 45, which covers portions of Sheepshead Bay, Midwood, Manhattan Beach, Gravesend, and Brighton Beach in Brooklyn.

Originally from the former USSR, he worked in radio and co-founded the Russian-language station Freedom FM before winning the seat in November 2022 by defeating Democratic incumbent Steven Cymbrowitz.
His official biography says he plans to focus on crime, affordability of health care and housing, and quality of life.

paragraphs.text: Novakhov is originally from the former USSR, and his official biography says he immigrated to the United States with his family; Ballotpedia lists him as born in the USSR and living in Brooklyn.
He worked for 20 years in the radio business, and in 2019 he co-founded Freedom FM, which his official biography describes as the most listened-to Russian-language radio station in the country.
Novakhov won the Assembly seat on November 8, 2022, defeating Democratic incumbent Steven Cymbrowitz, 59.7% to 40.2%, and took office January 1, 2023.
He was re-elected in November 2024 over Democrat Joey Cohen-Saban, 15,383 votes (50.2%) to 15,151 (49.4%), a margin of 232 votes.
The Assembly website lists his committee assignments as Aging; Children and Families; Cities; Governmental Operations; Housing; and Small Business.

His official biography says he plans to work on rising crime, especially against Asian American Pacific Islander and Jewish communities, on making health care and housing more affordable, and on quality of life, and it describes Brooklyn as his hometown.
